assessment.summary: ABL1 is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged kinase targets in oncology, with 7 approved drugs, over 5,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 85 high-resolution crystal structures including ligand-bound complexes at sub-angstrom resolution. The target is primarily implicated in BCR-ABL1-driven chronic myeloid leukemia and is supported by a vast and active literature base exceeding 1,200 publications. Druggability confidence is exceptionally high across all dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 63.4 is relatively low, but this is superseded by extensive experimental PDB structures and does not affect druggability assessment
Resistance mutations (e.g., T315I gatekeeper) remain a clinical challenge; coverage of all clinically relevant mutant structures may be incomplete
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for all 7 approved drugs are not fully captured in the provided data
Emerging non-CML indications (e.g., CHDSKM syndrome from gain-of-function germline variants) may require distinct pharmacological strategies not yet well-characterised
Combination therapy contexts and resistance mechanisms beyond point mutations (e.g., BCR-ABL1 amplification, alternative pathway activation) are not addressed in the provided evidence
